record.title: COMPASS reports decentralized language-model control for 1,024-agent flocking rollouts
record.summary: A robotics preprint presents COMPASS, which couples per-agent language-model reasoning states to a learned multi-agent spatial transformer (MAST) that exchanges local neighbor messages and generates both low-level actions and a feedback token. The frozen Qwen3-1.7B configuration is trained on 32- and 64-agent expert rollouts, then evaluated in 30-second flocking rollouts up to 1,024 agents. The authors report mean heading error decreasing from 2.79° at N=8 to 0.34° at N=1,024, with comparisons against a centralized Claude Opus 4.8 controller and a language-only communication ablation. This is an author-reported result on a narrow modeled flocking task; the paper does not report physical robot trials, and independent replication or artifact execution was not performed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: COMPASS couples local language-model reasoning states to a learned multi-agent spatial transformer (MAST), which exchanges multi-hop neighbor information and emits low-level actions plus a feedback token.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: With a frozen Qwen3-1.7B reasoning engine trained on N=32 and N=64 expert rollouts, the authors evaluate 30-second flocking rollouts through N=1,024 agents and report heading error decreasing from 2.79° at N=8 to 0.34° at N=1,024.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report comparisons with a centralized Claude Opus 4.8 controller and a language-only communication ablation; they report fragmentation and slower movement for the language-only method at N=64 and reduced coordination for the centralized controller as team size grows.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper reports modeled flocking rollouts and held-out prompt trials, but does not report physical robot execution, deployment reliability, or transfer beyond the tested flocking and direction-command setup.

evidence_gaps.description: The scale, heading-error and coordination results have not been independently reproduced, and no author artifact was located or executed in this review.
Physical robot execution, communication delay/loss, energy cost, safety and failure recovery are not established by the reported modeled flocking rollouts.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded rollout result is reproducible, decentralized learned coordination around language-model intent could change design choices for large simulated robot collectives. The evidence is one flocking task in modeled rollouts and does not establish physical deployment or broader transfer.
limitations: The paper reports modeled rollouts and does not describe a physical robot trial or hardware deployment.
Evidence is limited to flocking and direction-following; it does not establish transfer to manipulation, obstacle-rich navigation or heterogeneous fleets.
The 1,024-agent scale result is an author-reported rollout; no independent reproduction or artifact execution was performed.
The learned controller is trained on expert rollouts at N=32 and 64; transfer from those modeled training sizes to physical fleet behavior remains untested.
brief.summary: A robotics preprint presents COMPASS, which couples per-agent language-model reasoning states to a learned multi-agent spatial transformer (MAST) that exchanges local neighbor messages and generates both low-level actions and a feedback token. The frozen Qwen3-1.7B configuration is trained on 32- and 64-agent expert rollouts, then evaluated in 30-second flocking rollouts up to 1,024 agents. The authors report mean heading error decreasing from 2.79° at N=8 to 0.34° at N=1,024, with comparisons against a centralized Claude Opus 4.8 controller and a language-only communication ablation. This is an author-reported result on a narrow modeled flocking task; the paper does not report physical robot trials, and independent replication or artifact execution was not performed.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report evaluating 30-second rollouts at N=8,16,32,64,128,256,512 and 1,024 after training on N=32 and 64. In the cardinal-direction scale experiment, heading error decreases from 2.79° at N=8 to 0.34° at N=1,024. The language-only communication ablation fragments the N=64 flock into 15 groups and averages 2.5 m/s versus a 5 m/s target.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible preprint documents the method, modeled rollout setup, comparison policies, metrics and author-reported scale results. Performance remains claimed; the research desk did not execute the artifact or reproduce the results.
technical.mechanism: Each agent uses a frozen language model to derive a reasoning state from a prompt and pre-generated thinking trace. MAST aggregates local neighbor states with spatial attention, predicts low-level control actions, and returns a learned feedback token to the agent's language-model program. The default configuration uses Qwen3-1.7B, a 160-token trace, 1 Hz feedback refresh and a 10 Hz MAST control loop.
technical.novelty: Uses local language-model reasoning states and a learned spatial transformer for neighborhood-only coordination, returning spatial feedback into the language model's latent program instead of centralizing action generation or placing raw neighbor coordinates in text.
technical.regime: A flocking/navigation task with natural-language direction commands, local neighbor communication and 30-second rollouts; default frozen Qwen3-1.7B; training team sizes N=32 and 64, evaluation up to 1,024; language-model reasoning refreshes at 1 Hz and the spatial control loop runs at 10 Hz. No physical robot deployment is reported.
technical.reproducibility: The full paper specifies rollout metrics, training/evaluation splits, comparison policies and repeated trials for selected prompt-diversity results. No independent reproduction or public artifact execution was performed in this review.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares with a centralized Claude Opus 4.8 controller using hand-engineered feedback and a language-only communication ablation; it also reports an expert-oracle comparison. The bounded scale results are author-run modeled rollouts, not physical matched trials.

brief.title: COMPASS reports decentralized language-model control for 1,024-agent flocking rollouts
brief.why_it_matters: If reproduced, the separation of semantic instruction interpretation from local learned coordination may offer a useful architecture for scaling language-guided multi-agent control beyond centralized action generation. The paper reports a large modeled team size, but the evidence is a narrow flocking rollout and does not establish deployment on physical robots or general task transfer.
